verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents Authorization Services as an explicit step beyond roles ("If role based authorization doesn't cover your needs"). These services provide resource-level protection, where a resource is the protected object, evaluated through UMA permission tickets and a Protection API. Policy types beyond role-based include JavaScript, time-based and regex policies, plus user-managed resource access. That satisfies the policy-based form of the story. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the authorization services, deeper documentation of how policies are evaluated beyond section headings, and any evidence of relationship-based (ReBAC-style) modeling.
